title: Brightmoor Tenant Homeownership

communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: Brightmoor Tenant Homeownership
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, MCL 15.231 et seq., I request electronic records concerning the Brightmoor scattered-site affordable housing developments constructed or operated by Northwest Detroit Neighborhood Development (NDND), including the city's tenant-homeownership pilot program.

Specifically, I request:

1. HOME financing: Original HOME loan agreements, promissory notes, mortgages, amendments, repayment schedules, forgiveness provisions, outstanding balance records and agreements governing the release or sale of individual houses.

2. Tenant-homeownership pilot: Program agreements, budgets, eligibility criteria, participant-selection procedures, financial underwriting, memoranda and agreements with NDND concerning the pilot involving approximately 16 households.

3. Debt repayment: Records concerning the approximately $450,000 in Community Development Block Grant funds reportedly committed toward debt held by another lender to facilitate tenant purchases, including the identity of the lender, funding agreements, payment records, payoff calculations and the amount allocated to each property.

4. Property-specific transactions: For each property considered for sale through the pilot, records identifying the address, proposed sale price, final sale price, outstanding debt, liens, required repairs, closing costs, public subsidies, payoff amounts, mortgage releases and closing status.

5. Program evaluation: Any final report, financial reconciliation, audit, performance evaluation or internal assessment of the tenant-homeownership pilot, including the number of completed sales and reasons other proposed sales did not close.

For property-specific records, I am seeking transaction and financing information, not residents' Social Security numbers, bank account numbers, credit reports or other sensitive personal financial information. Such information may be redacted.

Please provide responsive records electronically, including spreadsheets in their original machine-readable format where available.

If estimated fees exceed $50, please provide an itemized estimate before proceeding.

If records are withheld, please identify the applicable statutory exemption and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions.

Thank you,

Aaron Mondry

title: Brightmoor LIHTC Lease-Purchase and Property Release Records

communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: Brightmoor LIHTC Lease-Purchase and Property Release Records
communications.communication:
Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, MCL 15.231 et seq., I request electronic copies of the following records concerning these Detroit developments:

- Brightmoor Scattered Sites Phase I (MSHDA #1691)
- Brightmoor Scattered Sites Phase II (MSHDA #1692)
- Brightmoor Homes II (MSHDA #1688)
- Brightmoor Homes III (MSHDA #1689)
- Brightmoor Homes IV (MSHDA #1690)

1. Lease-purchase program records: All approved or proposed lease-purchase plans, tenant-purchase procedures, homeownership conversion plans, and documents establishing the conditions under which individual homes may be sold to tenants. Please include MSHDA Policy #5, any applicable versions or revisions of that policy, and guidance explaining the requirements for releasing individual LIHTC properties from regulatory agreements.

2. Individual property-release records: All applications, requests, approvals, denials, pending requests and correspondence concerning the release of individual homes from LIHTC regulatory agreements or extended-use restrictions. This includes the underlying documents associated with property-specific folders identified in MSHDA's prior FOIA production as "Lease Purchase in process," "Lease Purchase requested units," or "Waiting for Release." Please include property addresses, request dates, approval dates, conditions imposed and final disposition where maintained.

3. Financial requirements for tenant sales: Records identifying any mortgage payoff, partial release price, debt repayment, reserve contribution, transaction fee or other financial obligation required before an individual property could be sold. Please include payoff schedules, lender consent requirements, financing analyses and correspondence concerning financial obstacles to proposed sales.

4. Brightmoor IV correspondence: The October 22, 2025, email and associated attachments referenced in MSHDA's September 15, 2026, noncompliance letter for Brightmoor Homes IV, including correspondence concerning the requirement to obtain approval before marketing or selling homes.

5. Partnership and financing records: For Brightmoor Homes II (#1688) and Brightmoor Homes III (#1689), the original LIHTC applications, partnership agreements, final development cost certifications, permanent financing agreements and final sources-and-uses statements, to the extent maintained by MSHDA. 

Please include amendments or agreements addressing investor exits, sales of individual homes, or disposition of the developments after the initial LIHTC compliance periods.

I request records from each development's initial application through the date of this request.

Please provide records electronically, preserving original filenames and attachments where possible. If estimated fees exceed $50, please provide an itemized estimate before proceeding.

If any portion is withheld, please identify the applicable statutory exemption and provide all reasonably segregable nonexempt material.

I am a journalist researching the long-term outcomes of publicly subsidized affordable housing and tenant-homeownership programs in Detroit.

Sincerely,

Aaron Mondry

seq. ("FOIA"), I, Tracy Siska, on behalf of myself and the Chicago Justice Project (the "Project"),
respectfully request copies of the public records listed below from the District of Columbia

Code § 5-129.02 (formerly § 4-114) for the years 2023 through 2025.
FOIA B

described in FOIA A of this request.
FOIA C
1. Records maintained by the DLCP that show, or are sufficient to show, the name(s) of any

for the years 2023 through 2025. Please omit only such data, if any, that the law requires
be withheld.
8. Documents sufficient to identify or account for any data withheld from the case-level data
provided in response to request C7.

FOIA D

officers for the years 2023 through 2025, and all Records created in response to those complaints,
including but not limited to investigative Records.
FOIA E

police officer appointed under 6A DCMR § 1100.1 or D.C. Official Code § 5-129.02 (formerly §
4-114) during the years 2023 through 2025.
FOIA F

police officers under 6A DCMR § 1100.1 or D.C. Official Code § 5-129.02 (formerly § 4-114)
within the District of Columbia for each of the years 2023 through 2025.
FOIA G

police officers under 6A DCMR § 1100.1 or D.C. Official Code § 5-129.02 (formerly § 4-114)
within the District of Columbia were renewed, suspended, or revoked, for each of the years 2023
through 2025, stated separately for each action.
FOIA H

commissioned under 6A DCMR § 1100.1 or D.C. Official Code § 5-129.02 (formerly § 4-114) are
required to complete.
FOIA I
Please provide copies of all Documents, including but not limited to the commission issued to each
special police officer, created or maintained by the DLCP in connection with applications submitted under 6A DCMR § 1103.3 by any individual or corporation seeking authorization for a
special police officer to carry a firearm, for the years 2023 through 2025.
FOIA J
Please provide all Records submitted to the DLCP related to the training that special police officers
are required to complete under 6A DCMR § 1103.3 to obtain or maintain authorization to carry a
firearm.
FOIA K
Records sufficient to show Your efforts to locate and produce the Records requested in FOIA A
through FOIA J above, including:
1. Where You searched for responsive Records and Documents.
2. Who searched for responsive Records and Documents.
3. Who was asked to produce responsive Records and Documents.
4. The identity of any Records and Documents that were located but not produced for any
reason.
INSTRUCTIONS
1. "Document" or "Documents" means any documents or electronically stored information of
any kind—including writings, drawings, graphs, charts, photographs, sound recordings,
images, and other data or data compilations—stored in any medium from which
information can be obtained either directly or, if necessary, after translation by the
responding party into a reasonably usable form.
2. "You" or "Your" means the District of Columbia Department of Licensing and Consumer
Protection, as successor to the former Department of Consumer and Regulatory Affairs
with respect to special police officers, and all of its attorneys, employees, officers, directors,
bureaus, offices, divisions, and subdivisions.
3. "DLCP" means the District of Columbia Department of Licensing and Consumer
Protection and all of its attorneys, employees, officers, directors, bureaus, offices, divisions,
and subdivisions. References to Records "created or maintained by," "received by," or
"submitted to" the DLCP also include Records created or maintained by, received by, or
submitted to the former Department of Consumer and Regulatory Affairs that are now in
the DLCP's possession, custody, or control.
4. 5. 6. 7. "Record" or "Records" means any documents or electronically stored information of any
kind—including writings, drawings, graphs, charts, photographs, video recordings, sound
recordings, images, databases, and other data or data compilations—stored in any medium
from which information can be obtained either directly or, if necessary, after translation by
the responding party into a reasonably usable form.
If You withhold any Record or information responsive to these requests, please identify
the Record or information in as much detail as possible and state specifically why each
Record or piece of information is being withheld, including the statutory exemption relied
upon.
If any Record is withheld on the basis of a claim of privilege, or of protection as material
prepared in anticipation of litigation or trial, please make that claim expressly in writing
and describe the nature of the Records not produced in a manner that will enable us to
assess the applicability of the privilege or protection. For each claim, please provide:
(a) the type of Record (e.g., letter or memorandum);
(b) the general subject matter of the Record;
(c) the date of the Record;
(d) such other information as is sufficient to identify the Record for a subpoena duces
tecum, including, where appropriate, the author, addressee, and any other
recipient, and, where not apparent, the relationship of the author, addressee, and
any other recipient to each other;
(e) the nature of the privilege or protection claimed; and
(f) if applicable, the litigation or trial in anticipation of which the Record was
created.
If any responsive Record has been lost, discarded, or destroyed, please identify each such
Record as completely as possible, including its date, general nature (e.g., letter,
memorandum, email, photograph, computer printout), subject matter, each author or
originator, each addressee or copy recipient, and its former custodian(s). In addition, for
each such Record, please provide:
(a) the date of disposal, loss, or destruction;
(b) the manner of disposal, loss, or destruction;
(c) the reason for disposal or destruction, or any explanation of the loss;
(d) the persons who authorized the disposal or destruction;
(e) the persons with knowledge of the disposal, destruction, or loss; and
(f) the persons who destroyed, lost, or disposed of the Record.
8. To protect the privacy of individual applicants, please anonymize all Records and data
produced in response to these requests by:
9. (a) removing the names of individual applicants; and
(b) reducing any personal addresses to the hundred block.
Please produce data in an electronic, machine-readable format (e.g., .csv or .xlsx) and other
Records in electronic form (e.g., searchable PDF), where available.
FEE WAIVER
Pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b) and 1 DCMR § 408, I request that all search and copying
fees associated with these requests be waived because furnishing this information is in the public
interest and will primarily benefit the general public. The Chicago Justice Project is a non-profit
organization focused on providing the public with transparency around justice system policies and
police conduct. The Project does not seek these Records for commercial purposes and will make
its analysis of them publicly available.
I look forward to your written response within fifteen (15) business days, as required by D.C.
Official Code § 2-532(c). Please direct all questions and responses regarding this request to me by
replying to this email at tsiska@chicagojustice.org.
Sincerely,
Tracy Siska
Chicago Justice Project

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Tracy Siska

The District of Columbia is required to respond to your FOIA request within fifteen (15) business days of its receipt.  See D.C. Official Code § 2-532(c)(2011).  However, under certain circumstances, D.C. Official Code § 2-532(d)(2011) authorizes the District to extend, by ten (10) additional days, the deadline by which it must respond to a FOIA request.  One of the circumstances provided by that statute is a case in which the District needs additional time to search for, collect and examine voluminous amounts of records and/or consult with an additional D.C. agency. 
For any questions regarding your request, please contact the FOIA office directly. Find the list of agency Open Government and FOIA contact information by visiting FOIA Contact Information. Regards, 
District of Columbia
